statement: Global data-centre electricity use in 2027 is below the IEA's 2025 base-case projection for 2027 (IEA; 2028 release)
status_at_phase_end: Data gap for the comparator (the IEA 2025 projection did not exist). As-of IEA view (2022 tracking report): global data-centre use 220-320 TWh in 2021 (~0.9-1.3% of final electricity demand, excluding 100-140 TWh crypto), only +10-60% since 2015 despite +260% workloads; expected to keep growing moderately over the next few years, longer-term highly uncertain; ML energy growth flagged but unquantified. Local hot spots were growing fast (one small market's data centres at 14% of metered electricity in 2021).

items.summary: The international energy agency estimated global data-centre electricity use at 220-320 TWh in 2021 (about 0.9-1.3% of global final electricity demand), excluding 100-140 TWh for crypto mining; up only 10-60% since 2015 while workloads rose ~260%, thanks to efficiency gains and the shift to hyperscale facilities.
items.detail: IEA Tracking report 'Data Centres and Data Transmission Networks' (2022 edition), Wayback Machine copy requested for 2022-12-15 (verified via web_extract this run). Table: data-centre energy use 200 TWh (2015) -> 220-320 TWh (2021); workloads 180 m -> 650 m; network energy 260-340 TWh (2021). Page text refers to September 2022 events, so the edition dates from Sept 2022 or later; exact publication day not verified. (month-only date)

items.summary: The agency's as-of outlook: data-centre energy use (excluding crypto) 'appears likely to continue growing moderately over the next few years, but longer-term trends are highly uncertain'; large data-centre energy use had been rising 10-30% per year; machine learning was flagged as a potentially significant but unquantified source of demand growth.
items.detail: Same IEA 2022 tracking report (verified via web_extract this run): ML training compute at one large platform growing 150%/yr and inference 105%/yr vs. its overall data-centre energy +40%/yr; another hyperscaler reports ML at 10-15% of its total energy use. No numeric 2027 projection given. (month-only date)

items.summary: A small non-top-3 market's statistics office reported data-centre electricity consumption up 32% in 2021, reaching 14% of national metered electricity (5% in 2015), illustrating fast local growth beneath moderate global totals.
items.detail: Bloc 34 CSO, 'Data Centres Metered Electricity Consumption 2021', statistical release 2022-05-03 (verified via web_extract this run; key findings page): quarterly consumption 290 GWh (Q1 2015) -> 1,058 GWh (Q4 2021); +265% Q1 2015 to Q4 2021. (month-only date)

items.summary: The indicator's comparator (the agency's 2025 base-case projection for 2027) did not exist at phase end, and the as-of report gave no numeric multi-year projection, so no YES/NO-relevant comparison is possible for this period.
items.detail: Gap stated against the IEA 2022 tracking report opened this run (no 2027 figure in the extracted text).
